atoms.text: Boudica was the queen of a tribe called the Iceni and led a famous rebellion against the Romans in AD 61. She was married to a client king called Prasutagus, who ruled the Iceni tribe.
atoms.sound: Boudica was the queen of a tribe called the Iceni and led a famous rebellion against the Romans in AD 61. She was married to a client king called Prasutagus, who ruled the Iceni tribe.

atoms.text: Before his death, he named the Roman emperor as joint heir to his kingdom along with his and Boudica’s two daughters. He likely hoped this would protect his family and kingdom from being seized by Rome.
However, when Prasutagus died, the Romans ignored his wishes. They took over all the Iceni’s land and publicly beat Boudica and her daughters.

atoms.a: Which two heirs did Prasutagus name before his death?
What did the Romans do after Prasutagus died?
b: ++They took over his land by force.
They organised a funeral for him.
They gave the kingdom to Boudica.

atoms.sound: What do you think Boodika decided to do next?

b.sound: She was so angry she led a huge rebellion against the Romans.
She didn’t mind the situation, and did nothing.

feedback.end: Boudica joined with other tribes and led the combined army against Roman cities.
feedback.sound: Boodika joined with other tribes and led the combined army against Roman cities.

instruction.text: Select the cities in the order Boudica attacked them. She started by sieging the Roman capital of Colchester.
instruction.sound: Select the cities in the order Boodicar attacked them. She started by sieging the Roman capital of Colchester.

atoms.instruction: Next, she sacked London, which had already been abandoned by the fleeing Romans.
Finally, she destroyed the wealthy city of St Albans.

finish.text: During her rebellion, Boudica targeted major Roman cities and ordered them to be burned to the ground. Back then, these cities were called Camulodunum (Colchester), Londinium (London) and Verulamium (St Albans).
finish.sound: During her rebellion, Boudica targeted major Roman cities and ordered them to be burned to the ground. Back then, these cities were called Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: While Boudica was attacking these Roman cities, the Roman army had been fighting the druids in Wales. Once they heard about Boudica’s revolt, they rushed back to England.

The exact location of the battle is unknown, but historians think it happened somewhere along Watling Street, a Roman road heading west from London. This clash became known as the Battle of Watling Street.
Boudica’s army was much larger than the Roman army. However, it consisted mostly of non-professional warriors, while the Roman soldiers were highly trained and had better equipment.
Ultimately, Boudica’s revolt was unsuccessful. The Roman army defeated Boudica’s warriors and the Romans remained in power for more than 300 years.

atoms.a: What was the Roman army doing when Boudica started her revolt?

b: the armies were the same size
++The Romans won and stayed in power.
The Roman army surrendered and escaped.

atoms.b: After being ((++defeated victorious)), Boudica is said to have poisoned herself to avoid being captured or killed by the Romans.
Boudica lived a long time ago and, as a result, details about her life and death are ((++uncertain clear)). However, the story continues to portray her as a powerful and fierce leader.

atoms.a: A bronze statue of Boudica and her daughters in a chariot can be found in central London.

feedback.end: Today, Boudica is a famous historical figure and a symbol of resistance.
